security_audit.summary: The skill primarily provides LibreOffice Writer documentation and examples. Several static hits are Markdown fence false positives, but the skill does instruct users to run soffice, pip, zip, unzip, and killall commands, and one template example inserts unescaped values into ODT XML.

remediation.issue: External command examples process local documents and archives.
remediation.suggestion: Document required user confirmation, validate file paths and formats, and keep subprocess calls as argument arrays without shell=True.

remediation.issue: Template variables are inserted into content.xml without XML escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Use an XML or ODF library to update text nodes, or escape every variable value before writing content.xml.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance uses killall and starts a local UNO socket.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before terminating processes and state that UNO sockets should bind only to localhost.

remediation.issue: Package installation examples do not mention dependency trust controls.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend trusted environments, pinned package versions, and normal package review before installing Python dependencies.

content.value_statement: Document teams often need repeatable creation and conversion without manual formatting work. This skill guides LibreOffice Writer workflows for templates, conversions, mail merge, and automation.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of ODT documents with LibreOffice Writer, UNO, and odfpy examples.
Shows format conversion between ODT, DOCX, PDF, HTML, RTF, TXT, and EPUB.
Explains template-based document generation from an ODT archive.
Describes mail merge and batch document processing workflows.
Lists command-line references and troubleshooting steps for headless Writer automation.
limitations: Requires LibreOffice or compatible tooling installed on the local machine.
Python examples require UNO bindings or ODF libraries in the active environment.
Conversion quality can vary by source document, fonts, and embedded objects.
Examples are guidance, not a packaged automation library with validation built in.

use_cases.title: Prepare Client Deliverables
use_cases.description: Create standardized ODT reports, then export final copies as DOCX or PDF for review.

use_cases.title: Automate Form Letters
use_cases.description: Generate repeated letters or notices from templates and structured recipient data.

use_cases.title: Batch Convert Archives
use_cases.description: Convert collections of Writer documents into distribution formats with consistent commands.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Writer Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writer skill to plan a new ODT report with headings, tables, metadata, and export steps.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Document Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writer skill to design a safe workflow for converting several ODT files to PDF and DOCX.

prompt_templates.title: Generate from a Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writer skill to outline a template workflow that fills variables, validates data, and produces a final ODT file.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Batch Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writer skill to specify a batch Writer automation process with error handling, logging, cleanup, and conversion checks.

output_examples.input: A team needs a quarterly report template and a PDF export workflow.
output_examples.output: A structured ODT report plan with sections, styles, metadata, validation steps, and PDF export guidance.

output_examples.input: An office has many ODT letters that must become DOCX files.
output_examples.output: A batch conversion approach that identifies source files, runs Writer conversion, checks failures, and preserves originals.

output_examples.input: A coordinator needs personalized notices from a shared template.
output_examples.output: A mail merge workflow covering data fields, template placeholders, review steps, and final document generation.

best_practices: Keep ODT source files and templates under version control when documents are generated repeatedly.
Use named styles, headings, metadata, and accessibility checks before exporting final documents.
Test conversions with representative documents before running batch jobs on important files.
anti_patterns: Do not run conversion commands on untrusted documents without reviewing the files and output location.
Do not replace template values inside XML without escaping or using an XML-aware library.
Do not assume PDF, DOCX, and ODT output will preserve layout identically.

faq.question: Does this skill create documents directly?
faq.answer: It provides workflows and examples for creating documents with LibreOffice Writer, UNO, odfpy, and templates.

faq.question: Which formats are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers ODT, DOCX, DOC, PDF, HTML, RTF, TXT, EPUB, and PDF/A workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with mail merge?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes mail merge and template generation workflows for repeated personalized documents.

faq.question: Does it require LibreOffice?
faq.answer: Most command-line and UNO workflows require LibreOffice installed with the soffice command available.

faq.question: Is batch conversion supported?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes batch conversion examples and encourages testing and failure handling.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code environments.
